# Predict scores of a PCA

Predict the PCA scores for a
[`gt_pca`](https://evolecolgroup.github.io/tidypopgen/dev/reference/gt_pca.md),
either for the original data or projecting new data.

## Usage

``` r
# S3 method for class 'gt_pca'
predict(
  object,
  new_data = NULL,
  project_method = c("least_squares", "simple", "plink", "OADP", "none"),
  lsq_pcs = NULL,
  block_size = NULL,
  n_cores = 1,
  as_matrix = TRUE,
  ...
)
```

## Arguments

- object:

  the
  [`gt_pca`](https://evolecolgroup.github.io/tidypopgen/dev/reference/gt_pca.md)
  object

- new_data:

  a gen_tibble if scores are requested for a new dataset

- project_method:

  the projection method: `"least_squares"` (the default, as done by
  smartpca), `"simple"`, `"plink"` (as PLINK 1.9), `"OADP"` (Online
  Augmentation, Decomposition, and Procrustes projection) or `"none"`;
  see Details.

- lsq_pcs:

  a vector of the indices of the principal components to use for the
  least squares fitting (and to return). Only relevant if
  `project_method = "least_squares"`. It defaults to all the components
  of the PCA.

- block_size:

  number of loci read simultaneously (larger values will speed up
  computation, but require more memory); by default, blocks of about 128
  MB.

- n_cores:

  number of cores

- as_matrix:

  logical, whether to return the result as a matrix (default) or a
  tibble.

- ...:

  no used

## Value

a matrix of predictions (in line with predict using a prcomp object) or
a tibble, with samples as rows and components as columns. The number of
components depends on how many were estimated in the
[`gt_pca`](https://evolecolgroup.github.io/tidypopgen/dev/reference/gt_pca.md)
object.

## Details

New individuals are projected on the loadings of the PCA, with their
genotypes centred and scaled as those of the PCA. The methods differ in
how they deal with missing genotypes:

- `"least_squares"` (the default): for each individual, the least
  squares fit of its standardised genotypes on the loadings of the loci
  genotyped in that individual (as `lsqproject` in smartpca).
  Individuals with many missing genotypes are not shrunk towards the
  centre of the PCA. With complete genotypes, it gives the same scores
  as `"simple"`. Individuals with too few genotyped loci to fit the
  components get `NA`, with a warning. As with `"simple"` and `"OADP"`,
  imputed genotypes are used only if the `gen_tibble` is set to use them
  (see
  [`gt_set_imputed()`](https://evolecolgroup.github.io/tidypopgen/dev/reference/gt_set_imputed.md)).

- `"simple"`: the product of the standardised genotypes, with missing
  genotypes set to 0 (the mean), by the loadings. An individual with a
  proportion f of missing genotypes is shrunk towards 0 by a factor of
  about 1 - f (e.g. to a fifth of its distance with 80% missing
  genotypes), so it should only be used with complete or imputed data.

- `"plink"`: the simple projection divided by the proportion of loci
  genotyped in each individual, which is how PLINK 1.9 projects the
  individuals outside the clusters of `--pca-cluster-names` (or
  `--pca-clusters`). It removes most of the shrinkage of `"simple"`.
  PLINK standardises the genotypes with the allele frequencies of all
  the individuals in its run, reference and projected, whereas
  [`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html) uses those of the
  PCA (see
  [`gt_pca()`](https://evolecolgroup.github.io/tidypopgen/dev/reference/gt_pca.md)
  to choose them): the scores are the same as PLINK's when the PCA uses
  the same frequencies, and PLINK's `.eigenvec` values are these scores
  divided by the singular values (`object$d`). Individuals with no
  genotyped locus get `NA`.

- `"OADP"`: the Online Augmentation, Decomposition, and Procrustes
  projection (Zhang et al. 2020), which corrects the shrinkage of
  projections with many more loci than individuals; missing genotypes
  are set to 0, as for `"simple"`, with the same shrinkage.

- `"none"`: the product of the genotypes by the loadings with
  [`bigstatsr::big_prodMat()`](https://privefl.github.io/bigstatsr/reference/big_prodMat.html);
  it needs complete or imputed genotypes (and uses imputed genotypes
  automatically).

In a simulation of individuals with 20-80% missing genotypes projected
on complete reference individuals, `"least_squares"` had no shrinkage
and the smallest error, `"simple"` and `"OADP"` shrank individuals by
their proportion of missing genotypes, and imputing the genotypes (by
their mode) before a simple projection only halved the shrinkage.
`"plink"` was close to `"least_squares"` with the frequencies of the
reference individuals, and had a larger error with those of all the
individuals, as PLINK does.

## References

Zhang et al (2020). Fast and robust ancestry prediction using principal
component analysis. Bioinformatics 36(11): 3439–3446.

Patterson N., Price A.L. and Reich D. (2006) Population structure and
eigenanalysis. PLoS Genetics 2: e190.

Privé F., Luu K., Blum M.G.B., McGrath J.J. and Vilhjálmsson B.J. (2020)
Efficient toolkit implementing best practices for principal component
analysis of population genetic data. Bioinformatics 36: 4449-4457 (for
the implementation of OADP in bigsnpr, which `"OADP"` uses).

## Examples

``` r
# Create a gen_tibble of lobster genotypes
bed_file <-
  system.file("extdata", "lobster", "lobster.bed", package = "tidypopgen")
lobsters <- gen_tibble(bed_file,
  backingfile = tempfile("lobsters"),
  quiet = TRUE
)

# Remove monomorphic loci and impute
lobsters <- lobsters %>% select_loci_if(loci_maf(genotypes) > 0)
lobsters <- gt_impute_simple(lobsters, method = "mode")

# Subset into two datasets: one original and one to predict
original_lobsters <- lobsters[c(1:150), ]
new_lobsters <- lobsters[c(151:176), ]

# Create PCA object
pca <- gt_pca(original_lobsters)

# Predict
predict(pca, new_data = new_lobsters, project_method = "simple")
```
